items.text: After dep-12, connections to cache were refused and the cart error rate rose sharply. Flipping the cartFailure flag contained the impact until a fixed build shipped.

Deploy dep-41 reduced queue partition throughput and consumer lag on queue grew steadily. Downstream consumers such as accounting and fraud-detection fell behind. A follow-up issue was opened against queue once the config was restored.

A recommendation release (dep-45) invalidated its cache in one go and the stampede slowed recommendation. Both product-catalog and frontend saw elevated request volume from the misses. Reverting dep-45 restored normal behaviour within minutes.

Deploy dep-51 altered astronomy-db settings; lock contention pushed product-catalog latency far above its band. Callers such as frontend, recommendation and checkout inherited the slowdown through their catalog calls. We rolled back dep-51 and the metrics returned to baseline.

A payment release (dep-80) broke charge handling and the checkout error rate jumped within minutes of the rollout. Users of frontend saw failed order placements for the duration. The on-call engineer flipped paymentGate, which isolated payment and stopped the damage.

Following dep-92, queue rebalanced consumers repeatedly and lag built up on the order topic. The accounting and fraud-detection consumers processed order events hours late. The previous settings were restored and a follow-up issue was opened to tune queue capacity.

A change to fct_revenue.sql (dep-95) altered how amounts were aggregated and kpi.exec_revenue jumped far outside its band. A data repair of fct_revenue.sql plus a rebuild brought the KPI back in band.

Deploy dep-96 shipped a new build of payment and charge calls started failing, which showed up as a spike in checkout errors. Users of frontend saw failed order placements for the duration. Flipping the paymentGate flag contained the impact until a fixed build shipped.

After dep-98 touched exec_revenue_metric.sql, the revenue KPI (kpi.exec_revenue) moved well beyond its trailing range. A data repair of exec_revenue_metric.sql plus a rebuild brought the KPI back in band.

Deploy dep-106 changed cache keys in recommendation, so the cache emptied at once and every request recomputed (a stampede). Both product-catalog and frontend saw elevated request volume from the misses. Flipping the recommendationCacheFailure flag contained the impact until a fixed build shipped.

Shortly after dep-108 rolled out to payment, checkout began returning failed orders to shoppers. Users of frontend saw failed order placements for the duration. A first attempt to flip paymentGate did not take effect, so the team rolled back dep-108 instead.

A change to stg_orders.sql (dep-116) altered how amounts were aggregated and kpi.exec_revenue jumped far outside its band. We reverted the transform, rebuilt the affected tables and re-ran the invariants before re-publishing the KPI.
